outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Crypto and rate-sensitive assets, led by Bitcoin and Ethereum
strongest.reason: Fed Governor Waller's dovish comments on holding rates steady sparked a sharp risk-on rally, with Bitcoin reclaiming $82,000 and heavy short covering fueling the move

strongest.area: Cybersecurity software, led by Zscaler's earnings beat
strongest.reason: Zscaler's strong fiscal Q4 results and raised guidance capped a week of solid cybersecurity prints, reinforcing confidence in enterprise security spending even as CrowdStrike faced its own leadership-transition headline

weakest.area: AI infrastructure mega-caps, led by Microsoft and Broadcom
weakest.reason: both pulled back after a strong recent run, with chip-tariff uncertainty and a broader pause in mega-cap tech taking some air out of the group despite no negative company-specific news

weakest.area: Robotics event-driven names, led by Tesla
weakest.reason: shares gave back their pre-event gains after the Cybercab launch failed to deliver a firm production timeline, underscoring how quickly event-driven rallies in this group can reverse

outlook.nextStep: The September 15-16 FOMC meeting is now the key catalyst to watch given Waller's rate-patience comments, while Tesla's Cybercab rollout is worth tracking for concrete production details rather than reacting to today's give-back. The semiconductor-tariff overhang remains a slower-moving, higher-uncertainty risk probably better monitored than traded on any single day's headlines.

signals.title: Fed's Waller signals patience on rate hikes, cooling September odds
signals.body: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he could support holding rates steady at the September 15-16 meeting if inflation continues to cool, pulling market-implied odds of a hike down toward a third-to-half range and sparking a broad risk-on move across stocks, crypto, and gold.
signals.focus: a meaningful shift worth tracking into the September 16 decision, though a single official's comments aren't the same as a committee decision

signals.title: Bitcoin surges to four-month high on Fed rate-hold hopes
signals.body: Bitcoin jumped roughly 5-7% to reclaim the $82,000 level, its highest since May, as Waller's dovish remarks triggered heavy short covering (roughly $415M in liquidations) and lifted the total crypto market cap toward $2.8 trillion.
signals.focus: a sharp, catalyst-driven move that's worth watching for follow-through rather than chasing after the fact

signals.title: Tesla's Cybercab launch underwhelms on timeline specifics
signals.body: Tesla officially unveiled the Cybercab, a 20-seat Robovan, and an upgraded Optimus at its "We, Robot" event, but shares that had rallied into the event gave back gains afterward as investors noted the lack of a firm production or rollout timeline.
signals.focus: worth watching closely for follow-up details on production timing rather than reacting to the initial event-day price swing

signals.title: Zscaler headlines a strong cybersecurity earnings week
signals.body: Zscaler beat fiscal Q4 estimates with 25% revenue growth, a record 24.3% operating margin, and raised full-year guidance, capping a week that also saw strong prints from CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks.
signals.focus: a fundamentally strong quarter that's worth watching for how the stock digests the post-earnings pop over the next few sessions

signals.title: CrowdStrike CTO departure adds to post-earnings profit-taking
signals.body: CrowdStrike shares slipped further after Bloomberg reported that CTO Elia Zaitsev is leaving to start an AI-focused venture fund, compounding a "sell the news" pullback that followed the company's record Q2 report and Fal.Con product announcements.
signals.focus: a leadership-transition risk worth watching for a successor announcement rather than a reason to react to the headline alone

signals.title: Semiconductor tariff uncertainty continues to weigh on chip stocks
signals.body: Earlier comments from Commerce Secretary Lutnick on incoming semiconductor tariffs continue to pressure chipmakers, with memory and AI-adjacent names like Micron and Broadcom showing mixed, choppy trading as investors wait for policy specifics.
signals.focus: a slow-moving policy risk probably better tracked for concrete details than traded on day-to-day headlines

signals.title: Enterprise software sector holds gains after Snowflake-fueled rally
signals.body: Software stocks remain up nearly 40% since the summer 'SaaSpocalypse' bottom, with Snowflake's strong Q2 print and raised guidance adding further fuel this week even as some individual names like Palantir and Adobe pulled back modestly.
signals.focus: worth watching whether the sector-wide strength broadens further or the recent leaders start to cool off
